can be rolled back instantly, whereas a structural error in a building is catastrophic."],"overturn_conditions":["If the 'building' (experiment) is so novel that no existing 'materials' (schema types) can describe it.","If the regulatory body (existing tool) forbids the specific 'design' (active learning pattern) entirely."],"shared_structure":["Innovation happens in the design (architecture/research loop), not the foundation (building codes/data schema).","Strict adherence to a foundational standard (schema/code) enables safer and faster iteration on the variable components.","Attempting to rewrite the foundation for every new design leads to collapse (data loss/fragility)."],"source_memory_refs":["Civil Engineering: Building codes vs. Architectural innovation"],"transfer_claims":["Just as architects use standard materials to build unique structures, researchers should use standard schemas to log unique experiments.","The 'integration tax' of adhering to code is lower than the risk of structural failure from ignoring it."]},"claim":"For a small team building a novel research tool with active learning loops, the optimal path is to adopt an existing experiment tracker but enforce a 'Schema-First' contract via a lightweight adapter layer, rather than building a custom tracker from scratch or using the tool without constraints.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the active learning loop requires sub-millisecond latency feedback that no existing tool's API can support even with an hours.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the team lacks the engineering bandwidth to maintain even a lightweight adapter layer alongside their core research code.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The mechanism is 'Constrained Integration': by defining a strict, versioned data schema (JSON Schema/Protobuf) before any logging occurs, the team creates a stable interface that decouples the volatile experimental logic (active learning loops) from the persistent storage engine. This allows the team to leverage the reliability and collaboration features of existing tools (addressing the 'migration cliff') while retaining the flexibility to hack the local adapter for novel workflow needs (addressing the 'integration tax').
